All queries run on the schema FAA, which has the fact table al_perf and the lookup tables. For
the delay questions (1, 2, 4 and 5) I only use flights that have a departure time, because
mysqlimport saved the empty delays of cancelled flights as 0.

## Problem 1

*Find maximal departure delay in minutes for each airline. Sort results from smallest to
largest maximum delay. Output airline names and values of the delay.*

```sql
SELECT a.Name AS airline_name,
       MAX(p.DepDelay) AS max_departure_delay_minutes
FROM al_perf p
JOIN L_AIRLINE_ID a ON a.ID = p.DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline
WHERE p.DepTime <> ''
GROUP BY a.ID, a.Name
ORDER BY max_departure_delay_minutes ASC;
```

```{python}
viz.table(viz.result(1))
```

```{python}
viz.q1_chart()
```

Southwest had the smallest maximum delay (610 minutes) and American the largest (3,125 minutes,
about 52 hours). Every airline had at least one flight that was more than 10 hours late.
[Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem1.csv)

## Problem 2

*Find maximal early departures in minutes for each airline. Sort results from largest to
smallest. Output airline names.*

An early departure has a negative DepDelay, so the earliest one is `-MIN(DepDelay)`.

```sql
SELECT a.Name AS airline_name,
       -MIN(p.DepDelay) AS max_early_departure_minutes
FROM al_perf p
JOIN L_AIRLINE_ID a ON a.ID = p.DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline
WHERE p.DepTime <> ''
  AND p.DepDelay < 0
GROUP BY a.ID, a.Name
ORDER BY max_early_departure_minutes DESC;
```

```{python}
viz.table(viz.result(2))
```

Alaska had the earliest departure, 56 minutes before schedule. Southwest never left more than
19 minutes early.
[Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem2.csv)

## Problem 3

*Rank days of the week by the number of flights performed by all airlines on that day (1 is
the busiest). Output the day of the week names, number of flights and ranks in the rank
increasing order.*

```sql
SELECT w.Day AS day_of_week,
       COUNT(*) AS num_flights,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS day_rank
FROM al_perf p
JOIN L_WEEKDAYS w ON w.Code = p.DayOfWeek
GROUP BY w.Code, w.Day
ORDER BY day_rank;
```

```{python}
viz.table(viz.result(3))
```

```{python}
viz.q3_chart()
```

Monday is the busiest day with 91,299 flights and Saturday the quietest. January 2024 had five
Mondays, Tuesdays and Wednesdays and only four of the other days, which is a big reason those
three days are at the top.
[Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem3.csv)

## Problem 4

*Find the airport that has the highest average departure delay among all airports. Consider 0
minutes delay for flights that departed early. Output one line of results: the airport name,
code, and average delay.*

`GREATEST(DepDelay, 0)` counts early departures as 0 minutes.

```sql
SELECT ap.Name AS airport_name,
       p.Origin AS airport_code,
       ROUND(AVG(GREATEST(p.DepDelay, 0)), 2) AS avg_departure_delay_minutes
FROM al_perf p
JOIN L_AIRPORT ap ON ap.Code = p.Origin
WHERE p.DepTime <> ''
GROUP BY p.Origin, ap.Name
ORDER BY AVG(GREATEST(p.DepDelay, 0)) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```{python}
viz.table(viz.result(4))
```

North Central West Virginia airport (CKB) had the highest average delay, 86 minutes. It only
had 15 departures in January.
[Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem4.csv)

## Problem 5

*For each airline find an airport where it has the highest average departure delay. Output an
airline name, a name of the airport that has the highest average delay, and the value of that
average delay.*

The CTE gets each airline's average delay at each airport, and `RANK()` keeps the top airport
for each airline.

```sql
WITH airline_airport AS (
    SELECT p.DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline AS airline_id,
           p.Origin AS airport_code,
           AVG(GREATEST(p.DepDelay, 0)) AS avg_delay
    FROM al_perf p
    WHERE p.DepTime <> ''
    GROUP BY p.DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline, p.Origin
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT airline_id, airport_code, avg_delay,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY airline_id ORDER BY avg_delay DESC) AS rnk
    FROM airline_airport
)
SELECT a.Name AS airline_name,
       ap.Name AS airport_name,
       ROUND(r.avg_delay, 2) AS avg_departure_delay_minutes
FROM ranked r
JOIN L_AIRLINE_ID a ON a.ID = r.airline_id
JOIN L_AIRPORT ap ON ap.Code = r.airport_code
WHERE r.rnk = 1
ORDER BY r.avg_delay DESC;
```

```{python}
viz.table(viz.result(5))
```

PSA at Syracuse has the highest value, 217 minutes. Many of these averages come from very few
flights. For example, Spirit's worst airport (Lafayette, LA) had only one Spirit departure.
[Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem5.csv)

## Problem 6a

*Check if your dataset has any canceled flights.*

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_flights,
       SUM(Cancelled = 1) AS cancelled_flights,
       ROUND(100 * SUM(Cancelled = 1) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_cancelled
FROM al_perf;
```

```{python}
viz.table(viz.result("6a"))
```

Yes. 20,389 of the 547,271 flights (3.73%) were cancelled.
[Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem6a.csv)

## Problem 6b

*If it does, what was the most frequent reason for each departure airport? Output airport
name, the most frequent reason, and the number of cancelations for that reason.*

```sql
WITH airport_reason AS (
    SELECT p.Origin AS airport_code,
           p.CancellationCode,
           COUNT(*) AS num_cancellations
    FROM al_perf p
    WHERE p.Cancelled = 1
    GROUP BY p.Origin, p.CancellationCode
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT airport_code, CancellationCode, num_cancellations,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY airport_code ORDER BY num_cancellations DESC) AS rnk
    FROM airport_reason
)
SELECT ap.Name AS airport_name,
       c.Reason AS most_frequent_reason,
       r.num_cancellations
FROM ranked r
JOIN L_AIRPORT ap ON ap.Code = r.airport_code
JOIN L_CANCELATION c ON c.Code = r.CancellationCode
WHERE r.rnk = 1
ORDER BY r.num_cancellations DESC, airport_name, most_frequent_reason;
```

The first 15 of 301 rows:

```{python}
viz.table(viz.result("6b").head(15))
```

296 airports had at least one cancellation. At 5 of them two reasons tie for first, so the
result has 301 rows. Weather was the top reason at 253 airports. Carrier was the top reason at
45, including Seattle, Newark, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Houston, which are Alaska and
United hubs.
[Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem6b.csv)

## Problem 7

*Build a report that for each day output average number of flights considering the current and
the previous two days.*

`ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` gives the 3-day moving average. January 1 and 2 use
only the days that exist.

```sql
WITH daily AS (
    SELECT FlightDate, COUNT(*) AS num_flights
    FROM al_perf
    GROUP BY FlightDate
)
SELECT FlightDate AS flight_date,
       num_flights,
       ROUND(AVG(num_flights) OVER (ORDER BY FlightDate
                                    ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS avg_flights_3day
FROM daily
ORDER BY FlightDate;
```

```{python}
viz.q7_chart()
```

```{python}
viz.table(viz.result(7))
```

The daily count goes from about 15,500 to 19,000 and drops every Saturday. The 3-day average
smooths this out and stays between about 17,100 and 18,500.
[Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem7.csv)
